result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_girth()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get girth (length of shortest cycle). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L40168-L40241){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_girth() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Girth](/assets/graphs/get-girth.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The house-shaped graph has cycles of length 3, 4, and 5. The shortest is the triangle A, B, C, drawn in the accent color, so the girth is 3." width="100%"} The girth is the length of the shortest cycle in the graph. Returns `None` if the graph is acyclic (a forest/tree). Uses BFS from each node to detect shortest cycles efficiently. The implementation includes fast-path checks: - returns `1` for graphs with self-loops - returns `2` for undirected graphs with multi-edges - returns `3` or more for cycles found via BFS ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Length of shortest cycle, or `None` if acyclic. - 1: Graph contains a self-loop (edge from node to itself) - 2: Undirected graph contains multi-edges (duplicate edges) - 3+: Shortest cycle length found via BFS - `None`: Graph is acyclic (tree/forest) ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Find girth of a cycle graph: ::: {#f9b61ddc .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "A")]) ) # Returns 4 (cycle length) graph.get_girth() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 4 ``` ::: ::: Self-loops have girth 1: ::: {#eef54154 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph().add_node(label="A").add_edge("A", "A") # Returns 1 graph.get_girth() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 1 ``` ::: ::: Triangles have girth 3: ::: {#d0a14d92 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A")]) ) # Returns 3 graph.get_girth() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: Trees have no cycles: ::: {#4633db8a .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} tree = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_balanced_tree(k=2, h=3) # Returns None (trees have no cycles) tree.get_girth() ``` :::
